newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank says wary of rising liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank says wary of rising liquidity.

text.p: Thai central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Monday his bank would monitor the Thai money market and its sharply rising liquidity this week to prevent big swings in domestic interest rates.

Rerngchai told reporters that while the authorities would allow general lending and deposit rates to move according to market forces, the central bank could influence short-term rates through its bond repurchase window.

"The Bank of Thailand would monitor against any excessive swings of interbank rates. We will not intervene in lending and deposit rates which should move in line with market forces although we could influence them through the R/P (repurchase) window."

Rerngchai made the statement amid market expectation that the scheduled launch of a 78 billion baht ($3 billion) Government Pension Fund (GPF) on Thursday could leave the market flush with funds and push down interbank rates.

The central bank, wary of excessive domestic funds being used by speculators to put pressure on the baht as happened early this year, on Friday tried to curb money supply by raising its weekly, one-month bond auction to 20 billion baht from a previously planned two billion.
The overnight interbank rate stood at 7.50-8.00 percent on Monday morning. Analysts did not expect it to fall below 6.00 percent soon.
Rerngchai said funds invested by the GPF could push short-term rates down but added: "Any decline to 3.00 percent would be considered excessive."
